headline: Bathroom Remodeling: Avoiding Common Mistakes Before You Start
articleBody:
Planning a bathroom remodel is exciting, but it's easy to overlook crucial details that can cause delays or headaches down the line. We want your project to be as smooth as possible! As a Berkeley resident, I prefer to work only in the East Bay Area, staying local and typically doing only one project at a time, ensuring my full involvement and attention to detail. Frasheski Construction does everything needed for a complete remodeling project, from the plumbing to cabinet installation, electrical, painting, and more.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- [ ] Beginning work before required permits are obtained — why it matters: This is a big one. Work affecting plumbing, electrical, structural elements, or ventilation often needs permits, and starting without them can lead to fines, stop-work orders, or even having to undo completed work. Always check local requirements first.
- [ ] Concealing uninspected plumbing or mechanical work — why it matters: Rough-in work needs inspection before it’s covered up by drywall or flooring. Skipping this can result in unsafe installations or compliance issues later.
- [ ] Failing to provide exterior ventilation — why it matters: Proper ventilation is key to preventing mold and mildew. An inadequate or non-existent exhaust system can compromise air quality and damage your new bathroom over time.
- [ ] Overlooking waterproofing during shower or tub installation — why it matters: This is critical for preventing leaks and water damage to surrounding structures. Inadequate waterproofing is a common and costly mistake.
- [ ] Ordering fixtures or tile too late in the process — why it matters: Lead times for materials can vary widely. Waiting too long to order can delay your entire project, especially with custom or specialized items.

How to use this checklist: Go through these points during your planning phase and before any work begins. Addressing these proactively will save you time, money, and stress, ensuring a successful bathroom remodel. Knowing what to prepare before you start can make a huge difference.
